A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Streaming Sliced Optimal Transport. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–D support comparison despite substantial reformatting and theoretical revisions.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gaussian simulations, ModelNet10 classification, ShapeNet gradient flows and MSRC-12 change-point detection results in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds Gaussian population-error checks, MNIST comparisons and computational timing results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The KKL sketch construction, CDF and quantile estimators, projected Wasserstein computation, Monte Carlo estimator, and one-sided and gradient procedures are retained. Revised guarantees and implementation disclosures do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds comparison of MNIST digit distributions: 5000 zeros versus 5000 ones in 784 dimensions. Gaussian, Gaussian-mixture, ModelNet10, ShapeNet and MSRC-12 coverage remains. The Gaussian experiment moved from the appendix was already present in v2.

E2.justification: The evaluated methods remain random-sampling SW, full SW and sliding-window SW in their respective comparisons. Added experiments reuse these methods. Online Sinkhorn and Compressed Online Sinkhorn remain discussed prior work rather than evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v4 adds closed-form Gaussian reference checks with L=10000, MNIST absolute-error evaluation, and runtime sweeps reaching two million samples. For retained sketch-size sweeps, the stated fixed n changes from 1000 to 10000; v2's figures already say 10000, so this reported correction does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a substantive computational scalability study in Table 7, testing runtime against stream length and sketch size, memory exhaustion, and the runtime effect of compaction frequency. This provides direct computational evidence beyond v2's retained-sample-count analysis. Existing accuracy sweeps and gradient-flow cases remain.

E5.justification: Both versions use ten-run approximation experiments, three-run gradient-flow summaries with ± values, and bootstrap-based detection thresholds. v4 extends existing reporting practices to additional accuracy results without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation procedure, seed specification, confidence interval or significance test.

E6.justification: v4 replaces the Gaussian and mixture error curves and adds Tables 4–7 covering population errors, MNIST and runtime. Table 6, for example, reports errors 0.000301 versus 0.003467 for Stream-SW and random sampling at M=100, L=100. Original Tables 1–3 are numerically unchanged. Ambiguous synthetic-setting documentation prevents interpreting revised curves as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Corollary 1 and Theorem 1 replace exponential probability guarantees with expected absolute-error bounds, with rewritten proofs in Appendices A.5–A.6. Proposition 4 now includes min{k1^2,k2^2,n,m}. Sections 3.1 and 3.3 revise compaction-time bounds, while Appendix A.1 changes the compaction-error derivation and corrects its concluding exponential bound.

C1.justification: Contribution 2 narrows the runtime claim from linear to nearly linear in stream length, matching the revised complexity analysis. The first-streaming-SW claim, memory advantage and principal downstream-performance contributions remain.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly frames Gaussian experiments as evidence beyond the compact-support theory. It adds practical qualifications: full SW is fast when data fit in memory, timings depend on implementation, and larger sketches can reduce runtime through fewer compactions. Much of the change-point interpretation was already in v2's appendix.

D1.justification: v4 discloses GPU/PyTorch implementation for full SW, pure-Python streaming compaction without optimization or parallelization, and the stages reflected in timings. Conversely, it removes v2's explicit Gaussian-mixture weights, means and covariance matrices. The code-access link and HP Omen 25L hardware description remain.

R1.justification: v4 adds the MNIST reference and recent optimal-transport and inference citations, including Truong and Nguyen (2026), while removing density-regression and multimodal application references. Positioning against Online Sinkhorn and Compressed Online Sinkhorn remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Sections 4.1 and 4.4 are rewritten, incorporating Gaussian and change-point discussion previously in Appendix C. There are localized explanatory corrections, corrected proof cross-references, author-year citations, and new impact and acknowledgement sections. Most introductory and methodological prose and the overall section sequence remain.

P2.justification: The main text changes to a two-column conference layout. v4 combines redrawn Gaussian and mixture plots into an eight-panel Figure 3, moves v2's appendix Figure 9 into main-text Figure 5, adds Tables 4–7, and substantially rearranges and resizes existing figures and tables.

improvement.justification: Tables 4–7 strengthen empirical assessment of accuracy and computational scalability, and Proposition 4 now accounts explicitly for finite samples. The main SW guarantees become weaker expectation bounds with expanded derivations. These gains support a limited net improvement, tempered by removed mixture parameters, unexplained synthetic-curve revisions and timing comparisons using different implementations.
